1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Bd.strategy: The main line: the bishop takes charge of e4 and eyes the kingside, while the knight on g1 still has its choice of square. White keeps the option of allowing or avoiding doubled pawns, and Black has to commit to a plan in the centre.
1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Bd.name: Nimzo-Indian Defence: Normal Variation

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Ne.strategy: Makes sure a capture on c3 can be answered by the knight, so Black cannot double the pawns. The cost is time and coordination: the knight sits in front of the f1-bishop and has to find a better square, while Black can build the centre in peace.
1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Ne.name: Nimzo-Indian Defence: Reshevsky Variation

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Nf.strategy: Develops the knight to its natural square, covers d4 and e5 and leaves the f1-bishop's square undecided. White allows ...Bxc3 to double the pawns, counting on the bishop pair and the centre; Black can now take the centre with a pawn.
1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Nf.name: Nimzo-Indian Defence

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.a3.strategy: Puts the question to the bishop at once: Black takes on c3, and White gets the bishop pair and a free hand in the centre for doubled c-pawns. Whether that is enough is the whole game, and White often cannot find the attack that makes up for the structure.
Takes at once: the bishop is attacked, and the exchange is the point of the defence. Black gives up the bishop pair to leave White with doubled c-pawns, a weakness to aim at for the rest of the game.

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Bd.strategy: The classical reply: a pawn takes the centre and attacks c4, so White cannot play e4 undisturbed. Black's pawns on d5 and e6 form a sturdy centre and the pin on c3 stays. White must soon decide how to resolve the tension on c4.
Attacks d4 at once and keeps the d-pawn flexible, so Black decides the central structure later. White has to meet the pressure by developing quickly, and the game can still reach the main line.

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Ne.strategy: Takes the centre and attacks c4 while White's bishop is still shut in by the knight on e2. Black does not count on doubling White's pawns here, because the knight can recapture on c3; the fight is for the centre instead.

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 O-O 5.Nf.strategy: Builds a solid pawn centre on d5 and e6 and keeps the pin, so e4 is hard for White to push. White has to decide how to deal with the pin and the pressure on c4, while Black reaches a familiar structure with the bishop already active.
